pages.text: Documentation that looks as good as it reads Build beautiful documentation locally with Paglora. Write in Markdown, design your website on a responsive canvas, and export portable static HTML for any host. No visitor account, subscription, or Paglora backend. Note This is a Paglora-built website, not a separate docs framework. Its navigation, cards, callouts, site theme, and content are authored in the same Paglora project described here. The official site is still private during development; GitHub Pages has not been deployed. Start building Get started Design your documentation See what you can publish A real documentation website, not a screenshot This project demonstrates the same features that your own documentation can use: Choose your path Writing your first documentation project? Go to Your first project. Customizing a website? Read Design site and Pages and navigation. Testing actual rendered features? Visit Markdown building blocks. Publishing to GitHub Pages? Start with Publishing a static website. Automating project setup? Use the npm CLI reference. Following development? Read What's new. Important The separately published paglora@0.0.1-alpha.3 npm package manages projects with init, inspect and validate. It does not export websites or install Desktop. Static export is currently performed by the desktop Studio. Paglora is open source under MIT. Find the source repository and report an issue.
pages.title: Welcome

pages.text: Installation and setup Paglora Desktop is currently a Tauri 2 early-development application with no stable Windows installer release. Run the Studio from the official source repository. Windows prerequisites Windows 11 with WebView2 and the Tauri 2 Windows C++ build prerequisites. Bun for the workspace and development commands. Rust and the appropriate Windows toolchain. Node.js 20 or newer for running standalone Node test commands. See the official Tauri prerequisites for the current setup. Launch the Studio Open the Paglora repository in GitHub Desktop, update to the current main, and run from its repository root: bun install bun run desktop The frontend-only bun run dev mode cannot access local project folders through Tauri. You can find the Studio project directory under Settings → Local project storage. Projects are stored locally, without an account. Public npm CLI The paglora@0.0.1-alpha.3 CLI is independently available: bunx --bun paglora@alpha --help bunx --bun paglora@alpha --version It can create, inspect and validate project folders. It cannot run the Desktop application or export websites. Tip If Windows PowerShell blocks npm.ps1, invoke npm.cmd instead (for example, npm.cmd view paglora@alpha version). You do not need to change the execution policy. Next: Create your first project or CLI reference.
pages.title: Installation and setup

pages.text: Your first project Use the Paglora Desktop dashboard to create and publish a local documentation project. 1. Create Select New project in Paglora Desktop and name it (for example, My Docs). Paglora creates a public Overview page and stores the project under its local application data directory. 2. Write Markdown Use Edit for the rich-text editor and automatically saved local content. Switch to Split for an editor-and-site view or Canvas to focus on the rendered website. Add ordinary Markdown, tables, supported callouts, code blocks and links. Public websites also enhance code blocks with copy buttons and headings with permalinks. 3. Organize pages In Pages, create additional guides. Assign a navigation group, choose a Docs, Wide, or Landing layout, and mark draft pages Private. Overview must remain public. 4. Design the website Open Design site to set the header, navigation, links, accent, default appearance, document language, and optional published site URL. Import a local PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF logo if needed. Use Source to customize theme/custom.css through Monaco. 5. Export and test Choose Website → Build static site. Paglora creates HTML, CSS, runtime JavaScript, search-index.json, fonts, and any referenced public local assets. If you configured a published HTTPS root, it also generates canonical links and a public-only sitemap. Serve the export through HTTP(S) to test search, appearance and code-copy interactions; the Studio canvas intentionally runs without site JavaScript. Important Your original docs/*.md files are source, not the upload destination. Only publish the generated website files; the project folder can contain private drafts. Next: Studio, Local images, and Publishing.
pages.title: Your first project

pages.text: What's new: October 2026 Paglora made substantial progress during October 30–31. These features describe the current development source, not a stable downloadable Windows installer. Desktop Studio 0.2.0 The 0.2.0 source milestone includes a publishing report after Website → Build static site, with: Counts of public pages exported and private pages excluded. A count of local images included in the successful export. Deduplicated warnings for public-page links targeting missing or private pages. Reminder to test browser interactions over HTTP(S) instead of file://. A warning does not silently change source content or turn private pages public. Website design Classic, Inset and Reading site layouts, with compatibility defaults for existing projects. Original, Graphite, Lavender and Linen site palettes for light/dark/system appearance. Independent accent selection in all modes and optional project-owned CSS. Docs, Wide and Landing layouts remain available per page. Publishing and runtime Bundled, minified browser scripts and MiniSearch, with prefix and typo-tolerant matching plus CJK substring support. Cards, callouts, code-copy controls, task lists, collapsible disclosures and responsive navigation. Import of PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF files (up to 5 MiB). Public-page-only image inclusion and search index generation. Document-language options (including Arabic RTL) and optional canonical URLs and sitemap. Public npm CLI paglora@0.0.1-alpha.3 is published under the npm alpha tag, with init, inspect and validate. It does not build websites; export currently requires Desktop Studio. What still needs work Manual Windows UI review and deployed-website checks remain necessary. Arbitrary MDX/TSX execution, one-click hosting deployment, full freeform canvas, and a stable Windows installer are not delivered yet. Next: Design site, Markdown building blocks, and Publishing.
pages.title: What's new

pages.text: Working in Studio Paglora Studio combines a local Markdown editor with a canvas-first website preview. The workspace Pages (left): select, create, reorder and organize documentation pages. Canvas (center): inspect the website's current rendering and selected content blocks. Properties (right): update page title, layout, navigation group and visibility. Switch between Edit, Split, and Canvas from the toolbar. Responsive preview Choose Desktop, Tablet, or Phone to check page layouts. Use the zoom controls and Fit to adjust the artboard to your workspace. The preview represents the generated HTML and CSS, not a separate mockup. Editing Select a supported block on the canvas. Simple unformatted headings and paragraphs support contextual or inline editing. Use Edit for nested lists, rich text, and links; Paglora avoids silently flattening unsupported formatting. The source files remain local and edits are automatically saved. Recent builds include safeguards against stale preview responses replacing a different selected page. Design site and local images Use Design site to manage header/footer links, content width, appearance, website accent, document language, optional published site URL, and logo images. The local logo import supports PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF files up to 5 MiB. Use Source to edit your project's theme/custom.css using Monaco. TSX/MDX component compilation is not supported yet. Preview versus published interactions For security, the inline canvas disables exported-site JavaScript. Search, appearance switching, code copying, and live TOC behavior should be tested on the built HTML served over HTTP(S). Site CSS and page structure remain visible in the canvas. Next: Pages and navigation, Search and appearance, or Local images.
pages.title: Studio canvas

pages.text: Design site: layouts, palettes and CSS Paglora's Design site panel changes the real documentation renderer used for both the Studio preview and the exported HTML. It is not a screenshot-only mockup. Choose your site layout Open a project in Desktop Studio, select Design site, and find the website layout choices: Layout Description When to use it Classic Familiar edge-to-edge documentation Existing projects and traditional navigation Inset Floating header and framed content A modern docs website with more separation Reading Quieter chrome and spacious typography Long-form guides and tutorials Changes appear in the Studio preview. Select Save layout to persist them to site.json. Note Website layout is different from per-page layout. In Pages, each page can still choose Docs, Wide, or Landing. The website layout controls the surrounding site shell. Coordinated light and dark palettes The palette presets are Original, Graphite, Lavender, and Linen. Each adjusts surfaces, text, borders and code blocks together for a cohesive site. Choose Light, Dark, or System for the default appearance, then adjust Website accent color independently. Your accent applies to links and active navigation in light and dark modes, including system-dark mode. Tip If an accent appears to stay blue in dark mode, inspect theme/custom.css. A declaration such as --brand: #72baff; inside a dark-mode rule overrides the picker. Remove that override to let the site accent work in both modes. Edit the actual project source Site settings live in site.json. New fields are optional and default to Classic/Original for existing projects: { "siteLayout": "inset", "sitePalette": "graphite", "themeMode": "system", "accentColor": "#5B9EFF" } The snippet shows the relevant fields only, not a complete replacement for your existing site.json. To apply extra polish, open Source and edit your project's theme/custom.css: /* Keep the accent and palette driven by Design site. */ .docs h1 { letter-spacing: -0.045em; } .docs a { text-underline-offset: 3px; } .docs pre { border: 1px solid var(--line); } Use palette variables such as var(--bg), var(--fg), var(--line) and var(--brand) rather than hard-coding one mode's color. Custom CSS is project-owned and exported with your site. Preview and verify Check Desktop, Tablet, and Phone widths. Compare Light and Dark; switch System while testing your OS preference. Save layout, then choose Website → Build static site. Open the exported website through HTTP(S) and test its appearance switcher. The Studio preview intentionally disables the site's JavaScript. Appearance persistence, search and other browser interactions must be tested on the published output. Next: Markdown building blocks, Studio canvas, and Publishing.
pages.title: Design site

pages.text: Pages and navigation A Paglora project has an Overview page at docs/index.md. Additional pages live under docs/, with their IDs, order, layout and visibility defined in pages.json. Organize pages Use the Pages sidebar to create, rename, duplicate, reorder, and delete pages. Set each page's navigation group and visibility in its Properties panel. Adjacent pages in the same group are displayed together in a collapsible published sidebar. This documentation groups topics under Getting Started, Studio, Features, Publishing, and Reference. Page layouts Layout Best for Docs Guides with sidebar navigation and a table of contents Wide Wider documentation content Landing Full-width introductory or overview pages Public and private A private page is omitted from exported HTML, sidebar links, local search and generated sitemap.xml. Overview always remains public, even if a manually edited manifest tries to make it private. Warning Privacy is a rule for Paglora's generated export. A raw project upload can still expose private Markdown and unreferenced assets. Do not deploy your project source folder. Links Link to other project pages using their Markdown filenames, such as [Studio](studio.md). Paglora rewrites supported .md links and extensionless internal Markdown links to the corresponding exported .html pages. For published headings, H2/H3/H4 anchors are shareable and support Unicode text. Next: Studio or Publishing.
pages.title: Pages and navigation

pages.text: Markdown building blocks This page is a live showcase of Paglora's own renderer. Everything below is written in ordinary Markdown in the source project; the same blocks render in the Studio preview and the static export. Documentation cards A documentation card Use a card for a clear next action. Try A second route Explore Cards can be inserted through the Card tool in Studio's block palette or authored in Markdown with a blockquote starting [!CARD] Title. Callouts Note Notes add context without interrupting the main guide. Tip Tips highlight a convenient workflow or shortcut. Important Important messages flag a required step. Warning Warnings help avoid mistakes, such as uploading raw private project files. Caution Use caution around operations that could affect published content. Callouts use the GitHub-style [!NOTE], [!TIP], [!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING], and [!CAUTION] markers at the beginning of a blockquote. Code blocks with Copy Published code blocks include a Copy action; the Studio canvas shows code without running browser scripts. bun install bun run desktop { "name": "Example Docs", "themeMode": "system", "accentColor": "#5B9EFF" } These commands launch the development Studio from the repository root. The JSON snippet is illustrative and not a complete project manifest. Tables and task lists Feature Exported behavior Public page Appears in navigation and search Private page Excluded from published HTML and search Page headings Shareable permalinks in published content Write Markdown content Choose the website design Test exported search and appearance through HTTP(S) Upload only the generated output Task-list checkboxes are visual indicators, not editable tasks on the public website. Headings and navigation The site's On this page outline reads page headings, and H2–H4 headings get shareable anchors on the exported website. For internal links, use Markdown such as [Design site](design.md). Paglora resolves these links to exported .html pages. Source compatibility Paglora supports Markdown and a deliberately limited set of documented block extensions. It does not compile arbitrary React components, MDX or TSX in exported docs yet. Insert native blocks in the Studio editor or edit the Markdown files directly. Next: Design site, Pages and navigation, or Search and appearance.
pages.title: Markdown building blocks

pages.text: Search and appearance Paglora exports readable static HTML plus two small, minified JavaScript files for client-side enhancements. No hosted search service or visitor account is required. Offline search with MiniSearch On a published site, select Search or press Ctrl+K (on macOS, Cmd+K). Enter a title, phrase, or word from a public page. Search supports prefix matches, typo-tolerant fallback, and substring matching for Korean, Japanese, and Chinese text. Use Up/Down to navigate results, Home/End to jump between results, Enter to open a page, and Escape to close. Keyboard selection and loading/error messages are announced accessibly. The dialog can retry if loading fails. The static export contains search-index.json with only public pages. The paglora-search.js browser bundle includes MiniSearch; no external CDN is needed. Search runs in the visitor's browser. The package's MIT notice is included in the exported licenses/ folder. Important A page marked private is excluded from navigation, search, the sitemap, and published HTML. This does not make project files safe to upload: only deploy the generated export, not the editable project directory. Appearance and accent The published header's Appearance control cycles through Light, Dark, and System. The preference is remembered where browser storage permits and can synchronize between open tabs on the same site. Choose your site's default appearance and Website accent color in Design site. The custom accent applies to both light and dark palettes, including system-dark mode, in current source builds. Project-owned theme/custom.css can override the built-in styles. The published site's appearance is independent of the desktop app's appearance. Page reading improvements The On this page outline tracks nearby headings in desktop and mobile views. H2, H3 and H4 headings offer shareable # permalinks, including Unicode headings. Code blocks have Copy controls with accessible progress and success/failure feedback. Markdown task lists and collapsible disclosure blocks render without an additional website framework. Callouts support NOTE, TIP, IMPORTANT, WARNING, and CAUTION. Preview versus published website Studio's inline canvas deliberately disables browser scripts for safety. The static HTML and CSS are previewed, but live search, appearance switching, and code-copy controls must be tested in the exported website served over HTTP(S). Opening index.html through file:// can prevent the search index from loading. Keep paglora.js, paglora-search.js, search-index.json, styles.css, and the rest of the export together. Do not upload just the HTML files. Next: Local images, Language and SEO, or Publishing.
pages.title: Search and appearance

pages.text: Local images and logos Paglora supports project-owned images for published documentation, without requiring a third-party image host. Import a local logo Open your project and choose Design site. Find Logo image URL and Import a local logo image. Select a PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF file (up to 5 MiB). Save the site settings. The logo URL will point into your project's assets/ folder. You can also use a valid HTTPS image URL for the logo, but an externally hosted image requires the visitor's network to reach that host. Use local images in Markdown Imported images live under your project's assets/ folder. You can reference their returned path from a Markdown document: ![Diagram of the documentation workflow](assets/my-diagram.png) Use the actual assets/... path returned when you import the file. Paglora accepts flat, safe filenames and the supported PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF image formats. SVG and arbitrary executable files are not supported as local imports. The current UI exposes a local image importer for the site logo. A broader image library and drag-and-drop media workflow are still future improvements. What gets published? The static exporter copies only local images referenced by public pages or the configured logo. Unreferenced local images and images referenced only by private pages are left in the project. This keeps static exports smaller and avoids accidentally including unused draft media. Warning Don't publish the entire Paglora project folder. It can contain private Markdown and unused assets. Publish only the generated website output. If an image is missing Check that the filename matches the imported path exactly, that the page is public, and that you rebuilt the website after changing it. Upload the entire assets/ folder from the latest generated export along with the HTML, CSS, and scripts. Next: Publishing a website or Troubleshooting.
pages.title: Local images

pages.text: Language and search-engine metadata Paglora can mark published documents with their language and generate useful discovery metadata for static hosting. Choose a document language In Design site, choose Document language. Current builds support 18 language options: English, Korean, Polish, German, French, Spanish, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Ukrainian, Arabic, Turkish, Italian, Czech, Hungarian, and Thai. This sets the HTML lang attribute and locale-aware social metadata. Arabic uses right-to-left document layout and adjusted navigation, lists, and tables. Note Language selection does not translate Markdown, create translated copies of pages, or add an automatic language switcher. Write your content in the selected language yourself. Set a published site URL Published site URL is optional in Design site. For production, enter the full HTTPS root with a trailing slash. For a GitHub Pages project site, include the repository subpath: https://yourname.github.io/your-repository/ For a custom domain, use the final HTTPS site root: https://docs.example.com/ Paglora uses this root to generate canonical URLs for each public page and a public-page-only sitemap.xml. If left blank, it does not emit canonical URLs or a sitemap. Incorrect roots produce incorrect URLs, so verify before deploying. Social previews and descriptions Published pages include title and description tags plus Open Graph and Twitter-card metadata. Paglora uses the configured site description and sanitized public-page content to provide useful page-specific descriptions. These are static tags, not a guarantee of search-engine indexing or rich previews. Search engines and social platforms decide how to display them. Deploying to GitHub Pages Build the site from Paglora Desktop. Upload or deploy only the generated export, keeping all page, CSS, JS, font, asset, and license files. Set the correct Pages path in Published site URL, then rebuild if the URL changes. Check sitemap.xml and a page's canonical link on the deployed site. There is no built-in automatic Pages deployment yet. The official paglora-docs project is still private and not publicly hosted. Next: Publishing a website or Search and appearance.
pages.title: Language and SEO

pages.text: Publishing a static website Paglora produces portable HTML, CSS, fonts, local images, and minified browser JavaScript. Visitors do not need a Paglora account or server. Build from Studio Save your documentation. In Pages, confirm which pages are Public. Open Design site to set navigation, appearance, accent, language, and optionally a published HTTPS site URL. Review the layout in Preview site. Choose Website → Build static site. A generated directory can contain: index.html studio.html publishing.html styles.css paglora.js paglora-search.js search-index.json sitemap.xml (only if a published site URL is configured) custom.css (if configured) assets/ (if a public page or logo uses local images) fonts/ (default Geist font and license) licenses/ (bundled MiniSearch MIT notice) Exact page HTML filenames follow your public page IDs. The exporter includes only public pages; private pages are also omitted from site navigation, search and the sitemap. Host the generated files Upload the contents of the generated export folder, not the original project source. Keep the scripts, JSON, fonts, licenses, and any generated assets/ together with the pages. GitHub Pages and other ordinary static hosts work. Serve through HTTP(S): browser restrictions on file:// can block loading search-index.json. Important A private page's Markdown may still exist in your local project. Never publish the entire project or the engineering reference/ directory. GitHub Pages project sites If your Pages URL is https://yourname.github.io/repository/, include /repository/ when configuring Published site URL. Paglora uses this root for canonical links and the optional sitemap.xml. Rebuild after changing the URL. Publishing remains a separate step; Paglora does not automatically commit or deploy your output to GitHub Pages. Test the real website Studio's canvas disables runtime scripts. Before announcing a deployment, verify the hosted website's Search button and Ctrl+K, appearance switching, code-copy controls, images, mobile navigation, and internal links. Check that private pages do not appear in the generated output. See Local images, Language and SEO, and Troubleshooting.
pages.title: Publishing a website

pages.text: Paglora CLI The public npm package paglora@0.0.1-alpha.3 is published under the alpha tag. It creates, inspects, and validates local documentation projects. This is not a Desktop installer or website builder. Install or run without installing bun add --global paglora@alpha paglora --version Or run the published alpha directly: bunx --bun paglora@alpha --help The npm latest tag is separate from the prerelease channel, so use @alpha to get alpha.3. Create a project bunx --bun paglora@alpha init ./my-docs --name "My Docs" The target directory must not exist. It creates paglora.json, pages.json, docs/index.md, and theme/custom.css and will not overwrite an existing folder. Inspect and validate bunx --bun paglora@alpha inspect ./my-docs --json bunx --bun paglora@alpha validate ./my-docs Inspection reports pages, layouts, visibility and navigation groups. Validation checks the canonical v1 project format, required files and other rules without rewriting content. Alpha.3 includes stricter argument handling, Unicode label validation, and enforcement that the Overview page stays public. Windows npm PowerShell workaround On some Windows machines, PowerShell blocks npm.ps1 with an execution-policy error. Use the Windows command wrapper without lowering security settings: npm.cmd view paglora@alpha version npm.cmd dist-tag ls paglora What the CLI cannot do yet The CLI cannot render or deploy a static site. Use Website → Build static site in Paglora Desktop. CLI-created projects outside the Studio's configured data folder do not appear on its dashboard automatically; see Settings → Local project storage. The old prototype's Pageo manifest is unsupported. Never publish npm 0.0.1-alpha.3 again; future releases must have a new version. Next: Installation or Publishing.
pages.title: Command-line interface

pages.text: Troubleshooting My page does not appear after publishing Check that it is Public, then rebuild and redeploy the export. Overview stays public. Private pages are excluded from HTML, navigation, search-index.json and the sitemap. My CLI project does not appear in Studio The CLI can create a project in any new folder. Studio currently discovers local projects only under its configured application data projects/ directory, displayed at Settings → Local project storage. Importing external project folders is not automatic yet. I changed the accent but dark mode still looks blue Update to a current Paglora source build. An earlier exported-site stylesheet overrode user accents with blue in dark and system-dark mode. The newer renderer applies the selected Design site → Website accent color to light, dark and system appearances. Save the site design, rebuild, and redeploy. If a custom theme/custom.css overrides --brand, check that CSS as well. Updating the app alone will not alter an already hosted export. Search is missing or shows no results Make sure you uploaded paglora-search.js and search-index.json alongside the HTML. Only public pages are indexed. Search needs an HTTP(S) origin; opening the HTML via file:// can block requests for its JSON index. The search dialog offers a retry when loading fails. Korean, Japanese and Chinese queries have substring matching support; other languages use bundled MiniSearch with prefix and typo-tolerant matching. Search and appearance do not work inside Studio The inline canvas intentionally disables generated-site JavaScript. To test interactive features, build the site and serve the exported output over HTTP(S). The visible canvas layout is not a substitute for browser interaction testing. A local image or logo is missing Local imports accept PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF up to 5 MiB. Check the assets/... filename, whether the page is public, and whether the latest generated assets/ directory was uploaded. Unused or private-only images are intentionally omitted. My sitemap is missing or contains the wrong URL Set Published site URL to the full HTTPS root ending in a slash. For GitHub Pages project hosting, include the repository segment (for example, https://example.github.io/docs/). Rebuild after changing the URL. Without a configured root, Paglora intentionally skips sitemap.xml. The exported website does not match the preview Upload the entire latest export: page HTML files, styles.css, optional custom.css, scripts, JSON index, generated images, fonts and licenses. External Google Fonts or HTTPS images need network access. Test on the real deployed URL. npm commands fail in Windows PowerShell If you see a message about npm.ps1 being blocked by execution policy, use npm.cmd instead of npm. You do not need to disable PowerShell security. Text editing on the canvas is limited Use Edit for links, lists and rich or nested Markdown. Canvas inline editing intentionally handles only supported simple blocks so it does not corrupt formatted source. Report an issue Use the Paglora issue tracker. Include your build/version, OS, reproduction steps and relevant logs. Back up development projects before trying new builds.
pages.title: Troubleshooting
